editorial.headline: Government Archiving Is a Public Institutional Function
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers government institutions that build, preserve, classify and communicate physical and digital archives—and it is closed to foreign investment nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
Government archiving is the public work of making a record durable, intelligible and available. This activity covers archiving services carried out by government institutions to build, store and classify collections of physical or digital archives, then communicate them to the general public or to defined user groups. Its centre of gravity is not merely storage: it is the ordered stewardship of documents and collections so they can be found, understood and used.

The scope is broad within that public institutional setting. It includes public archive services for general users and particular communities such as students, scientists, staff and members, as well as the operation of government archives. It reaches from acquiring or collecting archives through identifying, inventorying, describing and classifying them. It also includes safeguarding collections: monitoring sanitary and climate conditions, maintaining security and safety, and undertaking rehabilitation. Archives may be communicated on site or remotely, alongside related cultural and educational activities that bring their value to wider attention. The record expressly includes the archiving of documents in paper and electronic form.

The registration picture is direct. The activity is described as one performed by government institutions, and the record identifies no business scale as open to it. Nationally, it is **TERTUTUP** for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 0%. There is therefore no foreign-investment route to register this activity under the national position recorded here. That conclusion follows from the stated PMA status and ceiling, rather than from an assumed operational requirement or threshold.

Bali is also recorded as **TERTUTUP**, so a foreigner cannot register this activity there today. The Bali position is not attributed to the province-wide PMA moratorium for low- and medium-low-risk activities: the record places this activity at medium-high or high risk and says it is not blocked by that moratorium. Its Bali treatment must instead be verified for the particular address. That address-specific verification does not soften the recorded Bali status; it explains why the moratorium itself is not the basis for the closure.
